title: Method for node ranking in a linked database
note: PageRank. Larry Page's original patent, assigned to Stanford and licensed to Google, now expired. Every link-counting mental model in SEO starts here.
action: Spend effort earning references from pages that are themselves referenced. Being cited is the game, not link count.

title: Ranking documents based on user behavior and/or feature data
note: The reasonable surfer. Links do not pass equal weight; the more likely a real user is to click a link, the more it counts.
action: Put the links you want to count in the main content where people actually click, not in the footer or sidebar.

title: Producing a ranking for pages using distances in a web-link graph
note: Ranking by link distance from a trusted seed set. Proximity to genuinely trusted sites beats raw link volume.
action: Chase links from sites the trusted hubs of your niche already link. One link two hops from a seed beats fifty from nowhere.

title: Anchor tag indexing in a web crawler system
note: Anchor text gets indexed with the page it points to, not the page it sits on.
action: Write anchors that describe the target page. Those words become part of how the target is indexed.

title: Agent rank
note: Reputation scores for named authors whose content is digitally signed. The patent SEOs cite when they argue author identity carries weight.
action: Publish under a real, consistent author identity everywhere. Same name, same profiles, linked with schema.

title: Modifying search result ranking based on implicit user feedback
note: Clicks and dwell time reweight rankings. This family is what the leak's NavBoost tables look like in patent form.
action: Win the click and the stay: titles that match the page, pages that answer in the first screen.

title: Evaluating website properties by partitioning user feedback
note: User feedback split apart to judge different properties of a website separately, instead of one blended score.
action: Audit engagement per template and section, not site-wide averages. Fix or cut the sections that lose people.

title: Deriving and using document and site quality signals from search query streams
note: Quality signals mined from what people type into the search box. People searching your brand by name is a vote.
action: Build reasons for people to search your name: a tool, a study, a stance. Brand demand is measurable quality.

title: Ranking search results
note: A site-wide quality multiplier applied on top of page scores. The inventor is Navneet Panda, the engineer the Panda update is named after.
action: Prune or fix your weak pages. Site-wide quality is a multiplier, so bad pages tax your good ones.

title: Site quality score
note: Computing one quality score for a whole site from query and click patterns. Site-level scores are not folklore; they are patented.
action: Plan quality site-wide, not page-by-page. Ask of every section: would users pick this by name?

title: Site quality score
note: The continuation of the patent above. Google kept investing in site-level quality scoring for years.
action: Nothing new here, and that is the point: treat site-level quality as a standing budget line, not a one-off fix.

title: Prediction of human ratings or rankings of information retrieval quality
note: Models trained to predict what human quality raters would say. Raters do not rank your site; they teach the machine that does.
action: Read the Quality Rater Guidelines like a spec. Models are trained to predict those judgements at scale, so build what raters would rate well.

title: Contextual estimation of link information gain
note: Information gain. A document scores on what it adds beyond documents the user already saw. The patent against me-too content.
action: Before publishing, name what your page adds that the current top results lack. If the answer is nothing, do not publish.

title: Duplicate document detection in a web crawler system
note: Duplicate clustering at crawl time, with one version chosen to represent the cluster. Canonicalisation existed before you ever set a canonical tag.
action: Consolidate near-duplicates yourself, one page per intent, or Google picks the canonical for you.

title: Phrase-based indexing in an information retrieval system
note: Anna Patterson's phrase indexing. Pages understood through meaningful phrases and which related phrases co-occur. Topic completeness has a paper trail.
action: Cover the related phrases a real expert would naturally use. Co-occurrence is measurable, thin coverage shows.

title: Sitemap generating client for web crawler
note: Generating sitemaps for the crawler from the site itself. Part of the engineering around the sitemaps protocol Google introduced.
action: Keep sitemaps complete, current, and free of junk URLs. They are crawler input, not decoration.

title: Method and system for autocompletion using ranked results
note: Autocomplete, ranked by popularity. The suggestion box is a ranking system of its own.
action: Mine autocomplete around your brand and topics. Those suggestions are ranked demand you can build pages for.

title: Computing numeric representations of words in a high-dimensional space
note: word2vec. Words become vectors and similar meanings sit near each other. The ancestor of every neural matching system in search.
action: Stop counting exact-match keywords. Write in the natural vocabulary of the topic; the vectors already connect it.

title: Attention-based sequence transduction neural networks
note: The Transformer. Not a ranking patent by class, but it is the architecture behind BERT and the models that rewrite queries and read passages today.
action: Write for meaning, not keyword slots. The models reading your page understand context, hedging, and fluff.

title: Scoring candidate answer passages
note: Scoring passages, not pages, to answer a query directly. The mechanism behind featured snippets and passage-level ranking.
action: Structure direct answers: question as heading, a tight 40-60 word answer, then the depth. Passages are scored on their own.

title: Providing knowledge panels with search results
note: The knowledge panel patent. Entities get a curated box, and ten blue links stopped being the whole page.
action: Feed your entity: consistent name and details everywhere, sameAs schema, and the citations that earn a panel.

title: Information retrieval based on historical data
note: The historical data patent. Document age, link velocity and registration data as signals. Ten years of sandbox arguments trace back to this one.
action: Grow steadily. Link spikes and sudden swings read differently from consistent history, and history is a signal.

title: Document scoring based on document content update
note: How much a page changed, how often, and how that feeds scoring. Updating content is measurable, and measured.
action: Update meaningfully, not cosmetically, and date honestly. How much changed and how often is measured.

title: Temporal-based score adjustments
note: Scores tuned when interest in a query spikes. Freshness gets a lever when demand does.
action: When your topic spikes, ship fresh coverage fast. Freshness weighs more exactly when demand rises.

title: Modifying ranking data based on document changes
note: Rankings revisited when the underlying documents change. What you edit after you rank still matters.
action: Keep improving pages that already rank. Edits after ranking are inputs, not cosmetics.

title: Search result ranking based on trust
note: Ranking adjusted by trust attached to entities and the labels they apply. Trust as a computed input, not a vibe.
action: Earn endorsements from sources your niche already trusts. Trust flows through labelled references, not claims about yourself.

title: Identifying gibberish content in resources
note: Language-model scoring to catch spun and stitched-together text. Google patented spun-content detection years before AI slop was a phrase.
action: If a page reads assembled rather than written, fix it or kill it. Language-model detection is patented, deployed tech.
